title: Nonzero sections on split-torus torsors yield effective kernel twists
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], and let $r\geq0$. Put $T=(\mathbf G_{m,k})^r$ [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type]. Let $q:P\to X$ be faithfully flat and of finite presentation [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with a right $T$-action over $X$ for which $(p,t)\mapsto(p,pt)$ is an isomorphism $P\times_kT\simeq P\times_XP$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and use tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] and sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. If $\Gamma(P,q^*L)\ne0$, then there is an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $N$ with $q^*N\simeq\mathcal O_P$ and $\Gamma(X,L\otimes N)\ne0$. No group law on $X$ or $P$, properness, smoothness, integrality, or algebraic closedness is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0EKK (lemma-complete-reducibility-Gm) and 0EKL (lemma-Gm-equivariant-module), iterated for a finite-rank split torus and glued on the base of a torsor. Agent-extracted section consequence, not a verbatim assertion of either affine lemma; fpqc descent of the rank-one character summands is the proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent in descent.tex.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-split-torus-torsor-frame-geometry] to $q:P\to X$. Its hypotheses are exactly the given faithfully flat finite-presentation map and the specified torsor isomorphism; no smoothness or separation assumption is needed for its frame-product conclusion. Obtain invertible modules $A_1,\ldots,A_r$ and an $X$-isomorphism $P\simeq\prod_i A_i^\times$. Regard $P$ as this simultaneous-frame scheme. For $r=0$ the same node identifies $q$ with $\mathrm{id}_X$.

source.place: Frame-product reduction, using descent.tex Tag 023T as supplied by the cited frame-geometry statement.

proof.text: For $n\in\mathbf Z^r$ set $N_n=\bigotimes_i A_i^{\otimes(-n_i)}$, with zero and negative powers as in [lem-sfb-frame-product-laurent-algebra]. That node gives the normalized algebra isomorphism $\phi:\bigoplus_nN_n\xrightarrow{\sim}q_*\mathcal O_P$. In particular, for any common affine trivializing chart and frames $e_i$, its $n$-th inclusion sends $\bigotimes_i e_i^{-n_i}$ to the Laurent monomial $z^n$, where the universal frame of $q^*A_i$ is $z_iq^*e_i$. This is the character decomposition with the sign fixed by evaluation, not by a choice of left versus right representation convention.

source.place: Tags 01M2 and 01LX; Laurent frame algebra and its evaluation normalization.

proof.text: Construct a sheaf map $\Phi:\bigoplus_n(L\otimes N_n)\to q_*q^*L$ by sending a local pure tensor $l\otimes a$ in the $n$-th summand to $\phi_n(a)q^*l$. The tensor and pullback definitions [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pc-module-pullback] make this balanced and compatible with restrictions, so it extends through sheafification and the coproduct. On an open $V$ with generator $l$ of $L$, identify $L|_V$ and $q^*L|_{q^{-1}V}$ with their structure sheaves using $l$ and $q^*l$. Each $L\otimes N_n$ then identifies with $N_n$, and $\Phi|_V$ is precisely $\phi|_V$. Its inverse on $V$ is multiplication by $l$ after $\phi^{-1}|_V$. These local inverses agree since they invert the same map, hence $\Phi$ is an isomorphism. This proves the required projection formula directly for an invertible $L$.

source.place: Tag 01LX and the definition of sheaf tensor and pullback; local rank-one calculation.

proof.text: Choose $0\ne s\in\Gamma(P,q^*L)$ and set $t=\Phi^{-1}(s)\in\Gamma(X,\bigoplus_n L\otimes N_n)$. For each $n$, the identity on that summand and zero on the others induce a sheaf projection $\pi_n$ from the sheafified direct sum; put $t_n=\pi_n(t)$. These projections detect zero: locally a section of a sheafified direct sum comes from finitely many summands, and if all projections vanish that finite sum is zero after restriction to a neighbourhood. Thus all $t_n=0$ would force $t=0$ by the sheaf uniqueness axiom and hence $s=0$. Choose $n$ with $t_n\ne0$. This uses local finite support only; no assertion about commuting global sections with arbitrary coproducts is needed.

source.place: Sheafified direct sum specified in the Laurent-algebra node; elementary coefficient detection.

proof.text: Set $N=N_n$. It is invertible: on an open trivializing the finitely many $A_i$, the tensor of the appropriate powers of their generators (dual generators for negative powers) freely generates $N$. The simultaneous-frame representation in [lem-sfb-split-torus-torsor-frame-geometry] gives universal frames $\tau_i:\mathcal O_P\simeq q^*A_i$. Tensor their powers $-n_i$, using dual frames for negative powers. This gives an isomorphism $\mathcal O_P\simeq q^*N$: on each trivializing chart it sends $1$ to $\bigotimes_i\tau_i^{-n_i}$, and its inverse is the dual evaluation. The maps glue because the universal frames are global. These local formulas use exactly the tensor-pullback and dual conventions of [def-pc-module-pullback, def-sc-invertible-module, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Finally $t_n\ne0$ is a section of $L\otimes N$, proving both conclusions. If $r=0$, $N=\mathcal O_X$ and this is the original section under $P\simeq X$.

source.place: Tautological frame evaluation on the frame open of the dual vector bundle, Tag 01M2; tensor and dual definitions.

The sheafified sum ⊕N_n has the monomial basis there, so q is affine and ⊕N_n ≅ q_*O_P as algebras. The sign is correct: evaluating e^∨ against τ = z q^*e gives z. The descriptions glue under a frame change e' = g e (z' = g^{-1}z). I tested r = 0, the empty base and nilpotent coefficients.
